Q: How do token limits, decoding settings and model capability profiles affect provider selection?
A: A model profile includes supported inputs, output modes, context accounting, tool semantics, deployment limits and evaluation evidence. A published context window does not establish usable evidence capacity after instructions, tools, history and output reserve are included. Decoding parameters change sampling behavior but do not create missing knowledge or enforce authorization. Compare providers on representative tasks, latency, cost, privacy and failure behavior rather than only parameter count or a leaderboard rank. Record the actual model revision and request contract.
Why: Two providers may both advertise tool calling while exposing different argument validation and streaming behavior. An adapter must normalize only genuinely compatible behavior and surface unsupported capabilities explicitly.
Risk: An opaque alias can change behavior without an application source change.
Trade: Portability benefits from explicit capability checks rather than pretending all models are identical.
Try: Build a provider comparison covering one success, one unsupported feature and one malformed output.
